item: WT vs mutant root batch confound
question: WT root libraries (sample_fastq RS1RM1SS01-08, curated under TorresRodriguez2021) form a separate library/sequencing batch from all 16 mutant root libraries (SG1TM1001-1016). Root genotype contrasts (het/hom vs WT) are therefore confounded with batch. N contrasts within het or hom are not affected. How to handle?
proposed_answer: Use N contrasts within each mutant genotype only; do not build root WT-vs-mutant contrasts (or flag them as batch-confounded). Leaf libraries of all genotypes share lanes, so leaf genotype contrasts are not batch-confounded by genotype.
evidence: BioSample sample_fastq: WT roots RS1RM1SS0x, het/hom roots SG1TM10xx; WT and mutant leaves share DRRS001/DRRS002; all roots NextSeq 550

question: Leaf lane batch DRRS001 holds every full-P leaf library and DRRS002 every low-P leaf library (all genotypes). N contrasts within P level are unaffected; P effects in leaf are confounded with lane.
proposed_answer: Build N contrasts within tissue x P level x genotype only.

question: Heterozygous (pho1;2a'-m1.1/+) plants are curated as a separate mutant genotype with their own N contrasts. Keep het as an N-contrast genotype, or drop it and keep only homozygotes?
proposed_answer: Keep both het and hom as separate genotypes (paper reports misregulation in het too); contrasts can choose.
evidence: BioSample genotype W22/pho1;2a'-m1.1 (het) vs pho1;2a'-m1.1/pho1;2a'-m1.1 (hom); paper Fig. S4 (heterozygous effects)

question: This sheet has only the 32 het/hom runs; the 16 WT runs of the same experiment are under TorresRodriguez2021. Any genotype contrast needs them from there.
proposed_answer: Leave WT under TorresRodriguez2021 (owner); reference them from contrasts.tsv when needed.
evidence: runs.tsv study_id/also_used_by; Methods: WT siblings analysed previously in Torres-Rodriguez et al. 2021
